Continue the public API (see PUBLIC_API_PROMPT.md). Stage 1 (keys, Developers page, limits, scopes) is done.
Now do stages 2–5, committing after each. Reuse existing pieces: lib/api/v1/keys.ts (hashApiKey,
looksLikeApiKey), repositories/apiKey.ts (findApiKeyByHash, touchApiKeyLastUsed), lib/api/v1/limits.ts,
lib/api/v1/scopes.ts, ApiRequestLog.

Stage 2 — lib/api/v1/handler.ts: apiRoute({ scope, costClass, input, output }, handler) doing, in order:
request id (X-Request-Id) → Bearer key (looksLikeApiKey → hashApiKey → findApiKeyByHash; 401 if
missing/invalid/revoked/expired) → plan via getUserPlan (computed from User.plan + Subscription.currentPeriodEnd
with isProSubscriberPlan — never rely on lazy reconcile; not Pro → 403 plan_required) → scope (403 forbidden)
→ rate limit (Postgres limiter behind a RateLimiter interface; X-RateLimit-* headers; 429 + Retry-After)
→ daily pipeline quota (429 quota_exceeded; count only accepted jobs) → zod validation (strict, 64 KB max,
400 with field details) → Idempotency-Key for pipeline POSTs (24h) → Neatlogs runWorkflow with
source "api", metadata { apiKeyId, requestId, plan } → ApiRequestLog + touchApiKeyLastUsed (≤1/min)
→ one error shape { error: { code, message, details?, requestId } }; 500s never leak internals.
Then the sync endpoints: /me, /stories (filters: region values that actually work, category, from, to, q;
composite opaque cursor on publishedAt desc, id desc; no city filter), /stories/{id},
/instruments/search, briefings list/get, research list/get, newsletters CRUD + pause/resume.
Newsletters: email is always the account's primary email (not in input); count against the existing
per-user newsletter limit. Output DTOs only, never raw Prisma rows.

Stage 3 — async: POST /news/briefings and POST /research/reports return 202 + job (ApiJob: id, type,
underlying record id, request hash, webhookUrl; status read live from the underlying record).
Add optional `source` param to requestNews / startStockResearch (default = current behaviour) and "api"
to RunSource. Briefing dedupe in the API layer: same user/date/scope with ALL params equal → 200 existing
job, "deduplicated": true, no quota; same user/date/scope with different params → 409 conflict with the
existing id. storyCount 1–12. GET /jobs/{id}. Webhooks: https only, block private IPs; HMAC-SHA256 with a
per-user secret (shown/rotatable on Developers page), X-DS-Signature + X-DS-Timestamp, 3 retries via Inngest;
use waitForEvent if pipelines emit completion events, otherwise poll every 10s for max 30 min.

Stage 4 — OpenAPI 3.1 from the zod v4 schemas (toJSONSchema + .meta ids into components), stable
operationIds (e.g. stories.list, research.createReport), tags, examples for every response and error.
Serve GET /api/v1/openapi.json (public) and a public /docs/api page (Scalar) with quickstart (curl, JS,
Python, "requires Pro"), auth & scopes, async jobs, webhooks (verification code), errors, plans/limits,
pagination, idempotency, versioning, changelog. CI check that the spec builds and every route has schemas.

Stage 5 — tests from the original prompt (keys, plan gating incl. downgrade/re-upgrade, scopes,
validation, ownership 404s, rate limit, quota, idempotency, dedupe 200/409, async flow with mocked
pipelines, webhook signature, contract tests against the OpenAPI schemas).

Don't change pipeline logic or existing internal /api/* routes. Finish with the endpoint table, docs URL,
an example curl session, and anything left out.

  id String @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid

  key    String
  method String
  path   String

/**
 * Every public API v1 operation: method, path, scope, cost class, input and
 * output schemas, documented errors. Route files bind a handler to one of
 * these with `apiRoute`; the OpenAPI document is generated from this list.
 *
 * Build-safe: schemas and metadata only, no server imports.
 */

import type { z } from "zod";
import type { ApiErrorCode } from "@/lib/api/v1/errors";
import type { ApiScope } from "@/lib/api/v1/scopes";
import {
  briefingListSchema,
  briefingParamsSchema,
  briefingSchema,
  createNewsletterBodySchema,
  deletedSchema,
  instrumentSearchResultSchema,
  listBriefingsQuerySchema,
  listResearchQuerySchema,
  listStoriesQuerySchema,
  meSchema,
  newsletterListSchema,
  newsletterParamsSchema,
  newsletterSchema,
  researchParamsSchema,
  researchReportListSchema,
  researchReportSchema,
  searchInstrumentsQuerySchema,
  storyListSchema,
  storyParamsSchema,
  storySchema,
  updateNewsletterBodySchema,
} from "@/lib/api/v1/schemas";

/** `read` and `search` count only toward the per-minute limit; `pipeline` also toward the daily quota. */
export type CostClass = "read" | "search" | "pipeline";

export type HttpMethod = "GET" | "POST" | "PATCH" | "DELETE";

export type EndpointInput = {
  query?: z.ZodType;
  params?: z.ZodType;
  body?: z.ZodType;
};

export type EndpointResponse = {
  status: number;
  description: string;
  schema: z.ZodType;
};

export type EndpointDef<
  I extends EndpointInput = EndpointInput,
  O extends z.ZodType = z.ZodType,
> = {
  method: HttpMethod;
  /** OpenAPI path under `/api/v1`, e.g. `/stories/{id}`. */
  path: string;
  operationId: string;
  summary: string;
  description?: string;
  tags: string[];
  /** Required key scope; null = any valid key. */
  scope: ApiScope | null;
  costClass: CostClass;
  input: I;
  output: O;
  successStatus: number;
  successDescription: string;
  /** Other success responses with their own schema (e.g. 200 dedupe next to 202). */
  extraResponses?: EndpointResponse[];
  /** Accepts `Idempotency-Key`. */
  idempotent?: boolean;
  /** Endpoint-specific errors, on top of the ones every endpoint can return. */
  errors: ApiErrorCode[];
};

function defineEndpoint<I extends EndpointInput, O extends z.ZodType>(
  def: EndpointDef<I, O>,
): EndpointDef<I, O> {
  return def;
}

/** Errors any authenticated endpoint can return. */
export const COMMON_ERRORS: ApiErrorCode[] = [
  "unauthorized",
  "plan_required",
  "forbidden",
  "rate_limited",
  "internal_error",
];

export const endpoints = {
  me: defineEndpoint({
    method: "GET",
    path: "/me",
    operationId: "me.get",
    summary: "Current key, plan, limits and quota",
    tags: ["Account"],
    scope: null,
    costClass: "read",
    input: {},
    output: meSchema,
    successStatus: 200,
    successDescription: "The key's account, plan, limits and today's pipeline usage.",
    errors: [],
  }),

  listStories: defineEndpoint({
    method: "GET",
    path: "/stories",
    operationId: "stories.list",
    summary: "List public stories",
    description:
      "Public stories (from successful briefings and published community stories), newest first by `publishedAt`, then `id`. Stories without a publish time come last.",
    tags: ["Stories"],
    scope: "news:read",
    costClass: "read",
    input: { query: listStoriesQuerySchema },
    output: storyListSchema,
    successStatus: 200,
    successDescription: "One page of stories.",
    errors: ["invalid_request"],
  }),

  getStory: defineEndpoint({
    method: "GET",
    path: "/stories/{id}",
    operationId: "stories.get",
    summary: "Get a public story",
    tags: ["Stories"],
    scope: "news:read",
    costClass: "read",
    input: { params: storyParamsSchema },
    output: storySchema,
    successStatus: 200,
    successDescription: "The story with its full content.",
    errors: ["invalid_request", "not_found"],
  }),

  searchInstruments: defineEndpoint({
    method: "GET",
    path: "/instruments/search",
    operationId: "instruments.search",
    summary: "Search stocks, ETFs and mutual funds",
    description: "Indian listed instruments (NSE/BSE equity segments). Use `instrumentKey` to start research.",
    tags: ["Instruments"],
    scope: "instruments:read",
    costClass: "search",
    input: { query: searchInstrumentsQuerySchema },
    output: instrumentSearchResultSchema,
    successStatus: 200,
    successDescription: "Matches, best first.",
    errors: ["invalid_request"],
  }),

  listBriefings: defineEndpoint({
    method: "GET",
    path: "/news/briefings",
    operationId: "briefings.list",
    summary: "List your briefings",
    description: "Briefings you requested (web or API), newest first.",
    tags: ["Briefings"],
    scope: "news:read",
    costClass: "read",
    input: { query: listBriefingsQuerySchema },
    output: briefingListSchema,
    successStatus: 200,
    successDescription: "One page of briefings.",
    errors: ["invalid_request"],
  }),

  getBriefing: defineEndpoint({
    method: "GET",
    path: "/news/briefings/{id}",
    operationId: "briefings.get",
    summary: "Get a briefing and its stories",
    tags: ["Briefings"],
    scope: "news:read",
    costClass: "read",
    input: { params: briefingParamsSchema },
    output: briefingSchema,
    successStatus: 200,
    successDescription: "The briefing; `stories` is filled once it has succeeded.",
    errors: ["invalid_request", "not_found"],
  }),

  listResearch: defineEndpoint({
    method: "GET",
    path: "/research/reports",
    operationId: "research.listReports",
    summary: "List your research reports",
    tags: ["Research"],
    scope: "research:read",
    costClass: "read",
    input: { query: listResearchQuerySchema },
    output: researchReportListSchema,
    successStatus: 200,
    successDescription: "One page of reports, newest first.",
    errors: ["invalid_request"],
  }),

  getResearch: defineEndpoint({
    method: "GET",
    path: "/research/reports/{id}",
    operationId: "research.getReport",
    summary: "Get a research report",
    tags: ["Research"],
    scope: "research:read",
    costClass: "read",
    input: { params: researchParamsSchema },
    output: researchReportSchema,
    successStatus: 200,
    successDescription: "The report; `reportMarkdown` is set once it has succeeded.",
    errors: ["invalid_request", "not_found"],
  }),

  listNewsletters: defineEndpoint({
    method: "GET",
    path: "/newsletters",
    operationId: "newsletters.list",
    summary: "List your newsletters",
    tags: ["Newsletters"],
    scope: "newsletters:read",
    costClass: "read",
    input: {},
    output: newsletterListSchema,
    successStatus: 200,
    successDescription: "All your newsletters, newest first.",
    errors: [],
  }),

  createNewsletter: defineEndpoint({
    method: "POST",
    path: "/newsletters",
    operationId: "newsletters.create",
    summary: "Create a newsletter",
    description:
      "Sent to the account's primary email. Counts toward the per-account newsletter limit (shared with the web app).",
    tags: ["Newsletters"],
    scope: "newsletters:write",
    costClass: "read",
    input: { body: createNewsletterBodySchema },
    output: newsletterSchema,
    successStatus: 201,
    successDescription: "The new newsletter (active).",
    errors: ["invalid_request", "limit_reached", "payload_too_large", "unsupported_media_type"],
  }),

  getNewsletter: defineEndpoint({
    method: "GET",
    path: "/newsletters/{id}",
    operationId: "newsletters.get",
    summary: "Get a newsletter",
    tags: ["Newsletters"],
    scope: "newsletters:read",
    costClass: "read",
    input: { params: newsletterParamsSchema },
    output: newsletterSchema,
    successStatus: 200,
    successDescription: "The newsletter and its recent deliveries.",
    errors: ["invalid_request", "not_found"],
  }),

  updateNewsletter: defineEndpoint({
    method: "PATCH",
    path: "/newsletters/{id}",
    operationId: "newsletters.update",
    summary: "Update a newsletter",

    scope: "newsletters:write",
    costClass: "read",
    input: { params: newsletterParamsSchema, body: updateNewsletterBodySchema },
    output: newsletterSchema,
    successStatus: 200,
    successDescription: "The updated newsletter.",
    errors: ["invalid_request", "not_found", "payload_too_large", "unsupported_media_type"],
  }),

    method: "DELETE",
    path: "/newsletters/{id}",

## Endpoints (`/api/v1`)

| Method | Path | operationId | Scope | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/me` | me.get | any | read |
| GET | `/stories` | stories.list | news:read | read |
| GET | `/stories/{id}` | stories.get | news:read | read |
| GET | `/instruments/search` | instruments.search | instruments:read | search |
| GET | `/news/briefings` | briefings.list | news:read | read |
| POST | `/news/briefings` | briefings.create | news:write | pipeline, 202 |
| GET | `/news/briefings/{id}` | briefings.get | news:read | read |
| GET | `/research/reports` | research.listReports | research:read | read |
| POST | `/research/reports` | research.createReport | research:write | pipeline, 202 |
| GET | `/research/reports/{id}` | research.getReport | research:read | read |
| GET | `/jobs/{id}` | jobs.get | read scope of the job's type | read |
| GET, POST | `/newsletters` | newsletters.list / create | newsletters:read / write | read |
| GET, PATCH, DELETE | `/newsletters/{id}` | newsletters.get / update / delete | newsletters:read / write | read |
| POST | `/newsletters/{id}/pause`, `/resume` | newsletters.pause / resume | newsletters:write | read |

**Docs:** `/docs/api`, served locally at http://localhost:3000/docs/api. The Developers page also has a new card to show and rotate the webhook signing secret.

## Example curl session
```bash
K=ds_live_...; B=https://<APP_URL>/api/v1
curl $B/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $K"
curl "$B/stories?region=local&location=india&limit=5" -H "Authorization: Bearer $K"
curl -X POST $B/news/briefings -H "Authorization: Bearer $K" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -d '{"scope":"world","storyCount":5,"webhookUrl":"https://hooks.example.com/ds"}'
# → 202 {"id":"<job>","status":"pending",...}; Location: /api/v1/jobs/<job>
curl $B/jobs/<job> -H "Authorization: Bearer $K"            # pending → succeeded
curl $B/news/briefings/<briefingId> -H "Authorization: Bearer $K"
```

## Where I departed from the spec, on purpose
- **Quota check timing:** the daily quota is checked inside the pipeline handlers, just before a job is accepted, rather than in strict pipeline order. That way a deduplicated briefing or an idempotent replay still answers when the quota is used up.
- **Bad ids:** a malformed path id returns 404, the same as an id that belongs to someone else.
- **Idempotency storage:** only successful (2xx) responses are stored for replay, so a failed request can be retried with the same key.

# Public API v1: what's built

Pro users can call the product from their own code with API keys: read stories, request briefings and stock research, search instruments, and manage newsletters. Everything lives under `/api/v1`. It's built in 5 stages, all committed, and 57 tests pass.

## 1. Keys and access (stage 1, earlier)
- **Developers page** (`/settings/developers`): Pro users create keys with a name, scopes and expiry (30/90/365 days or never). The key is shown once; only its SHA-256 is stored. Revoke any time; up to 10 active keys.
- **Free users** see an upgrade card. If a user's Pro lapses, their keys are suspended (not deleted) and work again the moment they renew.
- **Scopes:** `news:read`, `news:write`, `research:read`, `research:write`, `instruments:read`, `newsletters:read`, `newsletters:write`.

## 2. Request handling (the same for every endpoint)
Each request goes through these checks in order:

1. **Request id:** your `X-Request-Id` is echoed if well-formed; otherwise one is generated.
2. **Key check:** a missing, invalid, revoked or expired key → `401`.
3. **Plan check:** computed live from the user's plan and subscription end date (with the 5-day grace period). Not Pro → `403 plan_required`.
4. **Scope check:** a key without the endpoint's scope → `403 forbidden`, naming the scope it needs.
5. **Rate limit:** 60 requests per minute per key, as a sliding window stored in Postgres (swappable for Upstash later). Every response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `-Remaining` and `-Reset`; over the limit → `429` with `Retry-After`.
6. **Daily quota:** 50 pipeline jobs per user per UTC day → `429 quota_exceeded`. Only accepted jobs count; deduplicated briefings and replays never do.
7. **Validation:** unknown fields are rejected, bodies are capped at 64 KB, and errors return `400` with per-field details. A malformed id returns `404`.
8. **`Idempotency-Key`** (on the two pipeline POSTs, kept 24h):
   - same key and same body → the original response is replayed;
   - same key, different body → `422`;
   - first request still running → `409`.
9. **Responses** pass through output schemas, so internal fields can't leak.
10. **Logging:** every request is written to `ApiRequestLog`, and the key's "last used" time updates at most once a minute.

Every error has one shape: `{ error: { code, message, details?, requestId } }`. A `500` never reveals internal details.

## 3. Read endpoints
- **`GET /me`:** the key, its scopes, plan limits and today's quota usage.
- **Stories:**
  - `GET /stories` lists public stories, filterable by `region` (local/world), `location` (e.g. "India"), `category`, `from`/`to` dates and `q` text search.
  - Pages use an opaque cursor, newest first.
  - `GET /stories/{id}` returns the full story.
- **Instruments:** `GET /instruments/search` finds stocks, ETFs or mutual funds on NSE/BSE. The `instrumentKey` it returns is what you pass to start research.
- **Briefings and research:** list and get your own, with a status filter. You can never see another user's (`404`).

## 4. Newsletters
- List, create, get, update, delete, pause and resume.
- They're always sent to the account's primary email; the API doesn't accept an email field.
- API-created newsletters count toward the same 5-per-user cap as the web app (`409 limit_reached`).

## 5. Async jobs (briefings and research)
- **Starting one:** `POST /news/briefings` or `POST /research/reports` returns `202` with a job and a `Location` header. The real pipeline starts, traced in Neatlogs with `source: "api"` plus the key id, request id and plan.
- **Status:** `GET /jobs/{id}` reports pending → running → succeeded or failed, read live from the underlying briefing or report.
- **Briefing dedupe:** there's one briefing per user, date, scope and location.

| Request | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Exactly the same parameters as an existing briefing | `200` with that job, `deduplicated: true`, no quota |
| Same slot, different parameters | `409` with the existing briefing's id |
| Same slot, but the earlier briefing failed | It's retried as a new job |

`storyCount` must be 1–12.
- **Webhooks:** pass an optional `webhookUrl` with the job.
  - It must be https, and private or internal addresses are refused, checked both when the job is created and again when connecting.
  - When the job finishes, Inngest sends one POST signed with HMAC-SHA256 (`X-DS-Signature`, `X-DS-Timestamp`), with 3 retries.
  - Inngest polls every 10s for up to 30 minutes; a job still running after that is marked expired and gets no call.
  - Each user's signing secret can be revealed and rotated on the Developers page.

## 6. Documentation
- **`/api/v1/openapi.json`:** a public OpenAPI 3.1 spec generated from the same zod schemas the server enforces. It has stable operationIds, tags, and an example for every response and error.
- **`/docs/api`:** an interactive reference (Scalar) with:
  - a quickstart in curl, JavaScript and Python, noting that Pro is required;
  - auth and scopes, async jobs and dedupe, and webhooks with verification code;
  - errors, plans and limits, pagination, idempotency, versioning and a changelog.

## 7. Tests and CI
- **`pnpm test:api:unit`** (32 tests, no database): covers every step of the request handling above, plus the rate-limit math, webhook signing and address checks, and checks that every documented example matches the spec.
- **`pnpm test:api`** adds 25 integration tests against the dev DB. They use throwaway users, and pipelines are mocked, so nothing is spent. They cover:
  - every endpoint end to end, including the async flow and webhook delivery;
  - dedupe `200`/`409`, ownership `404`s, the quota, and downgrade/re-upgrade;
  - every response validated against the OpenAPI spec.
- **`pnpm api:check`** confirms the spec builds and that every route matches its schema. It runs in a new GitHub workflow along with the unit tests.
